LESSON: VOLUME OF SOLIDS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.1 Area (8 lessons) • Area of a pentagon and a hexagon • Surface a
Topic 3.2: Volume of Solids
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Volume of Solids, part of Measurements 3.1 Area (8 lessons) • Area of a pentagon and a hexagon • Surface a in Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we determine the volume of different solids? 2. How do we use the volume of solids in real- life situations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Volume of Solids together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and Problem-solving: learner identifies and works out the volume of a frustum from a pyramid.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner identifies, discusses, and works out the volume of solids.

Values:
● Responsibility: learner takes care of the models of pyramids, cones, and spheres.

● Patriotism: learner collects objects from the environment to determine and discuss models/objects for different volumes of

solids.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Environmental Education: learner takes care of the environment while collecting the containers and objects.

● Safety: as the learner collects containers and objects cautiously.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Creative Arts and Sports: learner makes models of pyramids, cones/funnels, and spheres/balls from available materials.
